subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What default security and compatibility policy should OpenClaw use for externally or plugin-created recurring agentTurn cron jobs?
rationale: The evidence shows the current behavior is real, but changing it affects shipped cron defaults, bundled plugin APIs, model-cost policy, doctor/update UX, and quota enforcement, so automation should not choose the permanent boundary alone.

options.title: Consent-first recurring cron
options.body: Require trusted provenance and explicit user/operator activation for externally or plugin-created recurring agentTurn jobs, with model/cost preview and quota guardrails before they run.

options.title: Narrow cost-only guardrail
options.body: Keep current enablement semantics but require explicit model selection or warning/blocking when recurring jobs would inherit costly defaults.

options.title: Keep power-user default
options.body: Accept current auto-enabled plugin scheduling and track only narrower budget/provenance follow-ups, preserving compatibility at the cost of the reported runaway-usage risk.

recommendation.title: Consent-first recurring cron
recommendation.body: Require trusted provenance and explicit user/operator activation for externally or plugin-created recurring agentTurn jobs, with model/cost preview and quota guardrails before they run.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest recent routing signal for cron declarative jobs, plugin scheduled turns, and model-selection policy work.
